text: The stricter promise keeps every baseline recipient in the same course and seat type. Within our allowed shortlist family, the maximum additional enrollment coverage is exactly 314 hits.

text: The looser promise lets people switch schools, as long as everyone keeps a seat. We construct shortlists that gain 642 hits. The certified upper bound is 4,620.

text: Allowing switches gives us more than twice the demonstrated gain. But there's a wide gap to the upper bound. We haven't solved this problem to optimality.

text: The new shortlist must keep courses shared by the rank-blind and rank-informed policies. Its remaining slots come from the union of those two original lists. Its length stays fixed.

text: That constraint makes the comparison interpretable. It also sets the scope of the number 314. A platform allowed to add arbitrary new courses would face a different optimization problem.

text: The gap measures what the optimization has left unresolved. We have a concrete policy for the lower endpoint and a mathematical bound for the upper endpoint.

text: Protection covers every baseline recipient, including those without an enrollment link. Only the coverage objective needs that link.
spoken_text: Protection covers every baseline recipient, including those without an enrollment link. Only the coverage objective needs that link.

text: These are hindsight benchmarks: they use the evaluation cohorts' later enrollment labels to choose edits. A real policy wouldn't have those labels before assignment.

text: So we also test rules using only information available at that point.
spoken_text: So we also test rules using only information available at that point.

text: Here are two such rules. We freeze them after applications arrive and before the ordinary assignment. Neither uses that cohort's realized offers or later enrollment to select shortlists.
spoken_text: Here are two such rules. We freeze them after applications arrive and before the ordinary assignment. Neither uses that cohort's realized offers or later enrollment to select shortlists.

text: The structural rule restricts interactions around applicants without a guaranteed fallback. Its proof covers all permitted ordinary lottery orders, for the fixed inputs and reconstructed mechanism.
spoken_text: The structural rule restricts interactions around applicants without a guaranteed fallback. Its proof covers all permitted ordinary lottery orders, for the fixed inputs and reconstructed mechanism.

text: The proof starts with common options that already guarantee a pupil a seat. Around pupils lacking that guarantee, it freezes the relevant competitors and family interactions. This limits where edits can propagate.

text: We keep the same three cohorts and draw fresh priorities. There are 384 course-level cohort draws and 96 cohort draws using school and family tickets. This tests new lottery orders for the same applicants.

text: It gains 28 enrollment hits and has zero exits in the test panels.

text: The learned rule passes its design-panel checks and gains 50 hits. But it has one exit in each of two fresh test panels.

text: Twenty-eight is a small gain. What matters here is the difference between a proof covering the allowed orders and a rule that happened to pass many simulated draws. More testing alone doesn't turn the second into the first.

text: The retention guarantee still leaves a social-impact question. Protecting people who already have a place can leave everyone else out.
spoken_text: The retention guarantee still leaves a social-impact question. Protecting people who already have a place can leave everyone else out.

text: Our structural Chile rule has no new entrants on the reported paired test lotteries. It keeps baseline recipients placed, but doesn't expand access for those who were unplaced under the baseline.
spoken_text: Our structural Chile rule has no new entrants on the reported paired test lotteries. It keeps baseline recipients placed, but doesn't expand access for those who were unplaced under the baseline.

text: So the next objective must count both groups: the people we protect and the people still waiting for an opportunity.
spoken_text: So the next objective must count both groups: the people we protect and the people still waiting for an opportunity.

text: For a school district, that would mean reporting two columns at minimum. Of those who would have received a seat under the old policy, how many still get one? Of those who would have gone without, how many now have a seat?
spoken_text: For a school district, that would mean reporting two columns at minimum. Of those who would have received a seat under the old policy, how many still get one? Of those who would have gone without, how many now have a seat?

text: A rule can score perfectly in the first column while the second stays at zero.
spoken_text: A rule can score perfectly in the first column while the second stays at zero.

text: How people would act on our recommendations is an open question. They may ignore advice or add choices. Before deployment, they should be able to correct mistakes and seek human review or appeal.
spoken_text: How people would act on our recommendations is an open question. They may ignore advice or add choices. Before deployment, they should be able to correct mistakes and seek human review or appeal.

text: Those are proposed safeguards, not interventions we've tested.
spoken_text: Those are proposed safeguards, not interventions we've tested.

text: And keeping a seat may mean a worse school. Historical enrollment and modeled ranks aren't complete welfare measures.
spoken_text: And keeping a seat may mean a worse school. Historical enrollment and modeled ranks aren't complete welfare measures.

text: Recommendations can redistribute opportunities, but they cannot create affordable apartments or school capacity.
spoken_text: Recommendations can redistribute opportunities, but they cannot create affordable apartments or school capacity.

text: Even the structural rule's coverage gain is a net figure. In 115 applicant records the historical school appears for the first time. In 87 it disappears. None of those losses violates seat retention.
spoken_text: Even the structural rule's coverage gain is a net figure. In 115 applicant records the historical school appears for the first time. In 87 it disappears. None of those losses violates seat retention.

text: The mathematical promise protects placement status; it does not protect every useful option or every pupil's preference satisfaction.
spoken_text: The mathematical promise protects placement status; it does not protect every useful option or every pupil's preference satisfaction.

text: In a 2021 Chilean field experiment by Agte and colleagues, families were randomly assigned different versions of a school map. The basic version showed the schools.
spoken_text: In a 2021 Chilean field experiment by Agte and colleagues, families were randomly assigned different versions of a school map. The basic version showed the schools.

text: Another version gave counts by price and quality and highlighted inexpensive schools with medium or high official quality ratings. Families could apply anywhere.
spoken_text: Another version gave counts by price and quality and highlighted inexpensive schools with medium or high official quality ratings. Families could apply anywhere.

text: Compared with the basic map, the highlighted version raised application submission by three percentage points. It raised the share ranking a qualifying school second by 5.4 points.
spoken_text: Compared with the basic map, the highlighted version raised application submission by three percentage points. It raised the share ranking a qualifying school second by 5.4 points.

text: But the estimate for receiving any assignment was only 0.2 points, with an approximate interval from minus two to plus 2.4 points. That leaves both gains and losses plausible.

text: The outcomes use different samples. A qualifying second choice met the criteria. We don't know whether that particular school appeared on that family's map. The trial establishes that families can respond to information.

text: It doesn't tell us what would happen if everyone received our shortlists.

text: Here is a reason to care about that last distinction. Take a market with three pupils and three seats. The old rule shows the first two pupils school X, and the third pupil school Y. The new rule points everyone to Y.
spoken_text: Here is a reason to care about that last distinction. Take a market with three pupils and three seats. The old rule shows the first two pupils school X, and the third pupil school Y. The new rule points everyone to Y.

text: At Y, the second pupil has top priority, followed by the first and then the third.
spoken_text: At Y, the second pupil has top priority, followed by the first and then the third.

text: Imagine that each pupil independently has a one-in-four chance of receiving the new rule. For the first pupil, switching hurts only when the second pupil also switches.
spoken_text: Imagine that each pupil independently has a one-in-four chance of receiving the new rule. For the first pupil, switching hurts only when the second pupil also switches.

text: For the second pupil, switching helps when the first pupil stays with X and takes that seat. The third pupil sees Y either way. That gives individual effects of minus one quarter, plus three quarters, and zero.
spoken_text: For the second pupil, switching helps when the first pupil stays with X and takes that seat. The third pupil sees Y either way. That gives individual effects of minus one quarter, plus three quarters, and zero.

text: Their average is positive, one sixth.

text: Now switch everyone. Under the old rule, X and Y each filled a seat. Under the new rule, everyone competes at Y. Only one seat fills.
spoken_text: Now switch everyone. Under the old rule, X and Y each filled a seat. Under the new rule, everyone competes at Y. Only one seat fills.

text: A positive direct effect in a small trial coexists with a drop from two placements to one at full rollout.

text: A field test of the whole policy should therefore track everyone sharing those seats, including families who never changed their own list.

text: A shortlist reaches beyond the person receiving it. It changes who competes for the available places.

text: Our experiments make that interaction visible. Our theory asks what it takes to improve recommendations while protecting existing recipients.

text: Coordination can improve the totals. The harder design question is how to open opportunities for people without a place while keeping those who already have one matched somewhere. Thank you.
